record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Can the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms of a given closed manifold be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants, and is topological conjugacy a Borel equivalence relation on that space?

evidence.quote: Question 1.2 (Gorodetski). Can the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms of a given closed manifold be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants? Is topological conjugacy a Borel equivalence relation in the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ denote the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of $M$ ($r\ge 1$), endowed with the $C^r$ topology (a Polish space). A diffeomorphism $f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ is called Kupka–Smale if (i) every periodic point of $f$ is hyperbolic, and (ii) for every pair of periodic points $p,q$ of $f$, the stable manifold $W^s(p)$ and the unstable manifold $W^u(q)$ intersect transversely. Let $\mathrm{KS}(M)\subset\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ denote the set of Kupka–Smale diffeomorphisms, with the induced Polish topology. Define the topological conjugacy relation on $\mathrm{KS}(M)$ by
$$f\sim_{\mathrm{top}} g \iff \exists\,h\in\mathrm{Homeo}(M)\ \text{with}\ h\circ f = g\circ h.$$

Answer the following:
(a) Does there exist a complete classification of $(\mathrm{KS}(M),\sim_{\mathrm{top}})$ by Borel-measurable invariants taking values in a standard Borel space — i.e., a Borel map $\Phi:\mathrm{KS}(M)\to X$ into a standard Borel space $X$ such that $f\sim_{\mathrm{top}} g$ if and only if $\Phi(f)=\Phi(g)$?
(b) Is $\sim_{\mathrm{top}}$, viewed as a subset of $\mathrm{KS}(M)\times\mathrm{KS}(M)$, a Borel set?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent anti-classification work shows that on closed manifolds of dimension at least 5, topological conjugacy on $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is not a Borel equivalence relation, suggesting strong obstructions to a Borel classification by complete invariants. However, the question as posed specifically for the Kupka–Smale subspace (and for low-dimensional manifolds) does not appear to have been fully resolved in the literature, so it remains at least partially open.

status_evidence.title: Anti-classification results for smooth dynamical systems
status_evidence.snippet: For diffeomorphisms on manifolds of dimension at least 5, the equivalence relation of topological conjugacy is not Borel.
status_evidence.claim: Topological conjugacy on Diff(M) is not Borel in dimension ≥ 5, providing partial negative answers to the Borel question.

status_evidence.title: Classification complexity of chaotic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Anti-classification results show complexity of smooth conjugacy relations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results indicate strong complexity-theoretic obstructions to Borel classification of smooth dynamical systems up to conjugacy.
